faq_slots.question: Do you guarantee your work?

faq_slots.answer_brief: From [QUOTE_FREE] and [CV: quote_method].

faq_slots.question: How do your quotes work?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From [CV: quote_method] only.

faq_slots.question: How long does a garden landscaping project take?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Depends on size, groundwork and materials. Give the factors, not a number unless confirmed. Weather can move hard landscaping days.

faq_slots.question: Why does water sit on my patio or lawn after rain?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Use the assigned symptom's meaning and its linked local issue. Three genuinely different causes in plain words: ground underneath that drains slowly, a surface that falls the wrong way, no drain or soakaway to take the water. Then what the local ground adds, then the fix.

faq_slots.question: Is it better to lay turf or sow grass seed?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Turf gives a usable lawn sooner; seed costs less and suits larger areas but takes longer to establish. Timing matters for both.

faq_slots.question: What is the best time of year to landscape a garden?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Hard landscaping runs most of the year in dry spells; planting and turfing do best in autumn and spring. Booking ahead for spring.

faq_slots.question: Do I need planning permission for a patio or driveway?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Most back garden patios do not. Front driveways over 5 square metres need permeable paving or drainage into the garden, otherwise permission. Conservation areas add controls.

service_words_note: Old path only (21 Oct 2026): this list applies when the homepage is written from the uploaded custom values CSVs. A client with a v3 page map names every service by its page title (the services library's UK name), and this list is not used.

cards.title: Water that sits where it shouldn't
cards.brief: Puddles on paving, a soggy corner of lawn or beds that stay wet. The usual causes: a surface laid with no fall, a base that holds water, or ground that drains slowly. Say what the business checks first and what the fix usually involves, without promising the ground will change.

cards.title: Surfaces that sink or rock
cards.brief: Slabs that rock, blocks that dip, a step that moves. Cause: a base that was never compacted, bedding that was skipped, or edges with nothing holding them. Say what a sound base involves in plain words and that the fix starts underneath, not on top.

cards.title: Timber that fails early
cards.brief: Fence posts that lean, boards soft at ground level, a pergola post that moves. Cause: posts not set deep enough, timber sitting in wet ground, no gap for water to get away. Say what the business does differently at ground level.

cards.title: A garden that has outgrown its layout
cards.brief: Borders too close to paths, a hedge that blocks the way, levels that send water to the house. Cause: planting and levels set years ago for a different garden. Say how the business looks at the whole garden before it quotes one part of it.

cards.title: Getting to the garden
cards.brief: Rear access, a path down the side, where a skip can sit and how far materials are carried by hand. Say why a tight access costs more time.

cards.title: The materials you choose

faq_symptom.frame: [SYMPTOM]: why does it happen, and what can be done?
faq_symptom.answer_brief: The symptom and its linked local issue, answered as asked: the usual cause here in plain words, what the local ground or housing adds, then what the business does about it. One figure at most.

problem_card.title: Damage that shows after a wet winter
problem_card.brief: Lifted slabs, a leaning post, moss across the paving, a lawn that never dried out. Cause: water that sat all winter in a base or against timber, and frost moving what water had loosened. Say what the business looks for in spring.

faq_slot.question: Can you do [WORK_LOWER] work in winter?
faq_slot.answer_brief: What runs in the cold months (hard landscaping in dry spells, clearance, fencing) and what waits (turf, planting in frozen ground). No dates.

cards.title: A lawn full of moss and bare patches
cards.brief: Moss where the grass is thin and the ground stays damp, bare patches that never fill. Cause: shade, compacted ground, thatch, cutting too low. Say what a regular round does about each, from the trade facts.

cards.title: Hedges that have got away
cards.brief: A hedge wide at the top and bare at the base, growth over the path. Cause: missed cuts, cutting at the wrong time. Say how the round brings it back over more than one cut, and that nesting birds are checked for first.

cards.title: Weeds that come straight back
cards.brief: Weeds through paving joints and across beds within weeks of clearing. Cause: roots left in, bare soil with nothing covering it. Say what the round does so they stay away: roots out, soil covered.

cards.title: Borders that dry out or get swamped
cards.brief: Beds bare and dry by the first warm week, or sodden all winter. Cause: no mulch, planting too close, ground that holds water. Say what the round does through the year.

cost.h2: What Affects the Cost of [WORK] in [CITY]

cards.title: How often we visit
cards.brief: A regular round keeps on top of growth and costs less per visit than a catch up every few months. Visit frequency only from the confirmed practices; no promise of a schedule otherwise.

cards.title: The size of the garden
cards.brief: More lawn to cut and edge, more borders to weed, more hedge to trim. Say it plainly and give no figure.

cards.title: What each visit covers
cards.brief: A cut on its own against a visit that covers the lawn, the edges, the beds and the hedges. Say what is usually in a visit, from the card list.

cards.title: Green waste
cards.brief: Taken away or left for the council bin or the compost heap. Waste carrier registration only if [CV: waste_carrier_registered] is yes.
